newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-WEBSTER LEADS ORIOLES AFTER LEARNING OF DAVIS ILLNESS.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-WEBSTER LEADS ORIOLES AFTER LEARNING OF DAVIS ILLNESS.

text.p: Hours after learning that his good friend and teammate Eric Davis was diognosed with colon cancer, Lenny Webster delivered three hits and scored twice to help the Baltimore Orioles to a 5-4 victory over the Montreal Expos.
Roberto Alomar capped a three-run second with an RBI single and added a sacrifice fly in the fourth against starter Jim Bullinger (4-6) to snap a 3-3 tie.
Tony Tarasco led off the bottom of the eighth with a home run off reliever Lee Smith as the Orioles ended Montreal's 10-game winning streak.
The Orioles were told before the game that the mass removed in Davis's Friday colon surgery was malignant.

"We've got to go on as a ballclub, and we're going to keep Eric in our hearts and do the best we can," Webster said of the star outfielder before the game. "I saw him, he looks good and we're just gonna pull for him."
Scott Kamieniecki (5-3) allowed three runs and six hits over five innings for the win and five Baltimore relievers combined to allow one run over the final four innings.

In Chicago, Dave Martinez hit a two-run homer in the first inning and Doug Drabek allowed two runs and six hits as the White Sox avenged Monday's loss in the battle for the city's bragging rights by beating the Cubs 5-3.
Chris Snopek added a sacrifice fly in the second and a solo homer in the seventh for the White Sox. Sammy Sosa had three hits, including two doubles, for the Cubs.
The middle game of the interleague series between the cross-town rivals drew 44,249 fans, the largest crowd ever at the new Comiskey Park.

In New York, David Wells retired 15 straight batters and Derek Jeter's two-run double highlighted a four-run second inning as the Yankees beat the Mets 6-3 to even their hotly anticipated sold out subway series at Yankee Stadium.
Wells (8-3), who allowed three runs and six hits for the win, said: "This is a lot of fun. As a Yankee fans I want to beat those darn Mets."
Joe Girardi, Luis Sojo and Wade Boggs each drove in a run for the Yanks, who lost 6-0 Monday in the first ever game between the two New York clubs that counted in the standings.
Bernard Gilkey hit a two-run homer for the Mets.

At Minnesota, LaTroy Hawkins allowed three hits over seven innings in his first appearance of the season and all nine starters collected at least one hit and one RBI as the Twins crushed the Pittsburgh Pirates 13-1.
Pat Meares led the 17-hit attack by going 4-for-4, while Denny Hocking, Greg Myers and Scott Stahoviak each had two hits and two RBI for the Twins.

In Cleveland, Omar Vizquel drove in all five runs with a two-run single in the fourth inning and a three-run homer in the sixth and Brian Anderson gave up one run on five hits to lead the Indians to a 5-1 victory over the Cincinnati Reds.
Prior to Vizquel's two-run single off John Smiley (5-8), the Indians were 0-for-16 with runners in scoring position in the first two games of the intrastate contest.
In Boston, Darren Bragg had three hits and drove in four runs and John Valentin added three hits and two RBI as the Red Sox pounded out seven doubles in a 12-6 victory over the Philadelphia Phillies.
Nomar Garciaparra smacked a two-run homer in a three-run second and Boston broke open a 7-6 game with five runs in the seventh inning.
Aaron Sele (8-5) struggled through six innings but managed to get the win. Phillies starter Scott Ruffcorn took the loss.

In Toronto, Ryan Klesko belted a three-run homer and Mark Wohlers escaped a ninth-inning jam by inducing Joe Carter to bounce into a game-ending double play as the Atlanta Braves held on for an 8-7 victory over the Blue Jays.
Atlanta starter Greg Maddux (8-3) allowed three runs and seven hits before being replaced in the seventh by Mike Bielecki, who was rocked for four runs in two innings.
Shawn Green homered twice and Carlos Delgado added a solo shot for the Blue Jays.
In Detroit, Bobby Bonilla led off the ninth inning with a towering home run to give the Florida Marlins a 3-2 win over the Tigers, who remained winless in interleague play.
Detroit grabbed a 2-1 lead on a seventh-inning RBI triple by Curtis Pride. But Florida rallied for a 2-2 tie in the eighth when Gary Sheffield doubled home Kurt Abbot.
In the ninth, Bonilla drove a 2-1 pitch from reliever Todd Jones (1-3) off a light tower and over the right-field roof to give the Marlins their sixth win in seven games.
In Kansas City, Craig Biggio and Luis Gonzalez each drove in two runs and the Houston Astros were helped by five errors in a 10-2 romp over the Royals.
The game was scoreless until the Astros struck for six runs in the fifth inning, highlighted by Gonzalez's two-run single that extended his hitting streak to 21 games.

In Milwaukee, Jeff Cirillo's leadoff homer sparked a four-run sixth inning as the Brewers posted a 4-3 win over St Louis, spoiling the Cardinals debut of Fernando Valenzuela, who was acquired Friday in a six-player deal with San Diego.
The teams wore replicas of the uniforms they wore when they met in the 1982 World Series and played before 38,364 fans, Milwaukee's largest crowd since Opening Day.
